elements.element: Customer has a right to terminate for convenience
elements.evidence: 9.4 Customer may terminate this Agreement or any Order Form for convenience

elements.element: Notice period of 30 days' written notice
elements.evidence: upon thirty (30) days' prior written notice to Vendor

elements.element: Pro-rata refund of prepaid fees on such termination
elements.evidence: Vendor shall refund any prepaid Fees for the period after the effective date of termination

elements.element: Vendor has no termination-for-convenience right during a committed term
elements.evidence: Vendor has no right to terminate this Agreement or an Order Form for convenience during a term.
thirty (30) days' prior written notice (shorter than the 60–90 day fallback window)

elements.element: Early-termination fee not exceeding 3 months' fees
elements.evidence: No early-termination fee is imposed; "Customer shall have no further payment obligation for the terminated Services" — condition demonstrably absent

elements.element: Vendor may terminate for convenience only at end of a term on 90 days' notice
elements.evidence: "Vendor has no right to terminate this Agreement or an Order Form for convenience during a term." — no end-of-term Vendor right is granted (more protective of Customer, but not the fallback bargain)

offending_extra_words: except that the commitment is subject to Customer's termination rights under Section 9, including termination for convenience under Section 9.4, and ceases to accrue for periods after the effective date of any such termination
and Customer shall have no further payment obligation for the terminated Services
reasons: The inserted Section 9.4 completes every atomic element of the preferred position: a Customer convenience right, 30 days' prior written notice, refund of prepaid Fees for the post-termination period, and an express bar on Vendor convenience termination during a term.

Minimality fails on the Section 2.1 conforming edit: deleting the two words "or termination" from "without reduction or termination rights" would have removed the conflict, but the redline expands 9 words to 41 (changed-character ratio 0.769), adding a cross-reference and a new accrual mechanic that is not needed to complete the preferred level.

Secondary extra words inside 9.4 — "in whole or in part" and the additional "no further payment obligation" covenant — duplicate protection already achieved by the termination right and prepaid-fee refund.

Intent is preserved: the take-or-pay commitment, the cause-based rights in 9.3 and the severability/cumulative-remedy language in 9.5 remain effective, and no undefined term or dangling mechanic is introduced.

Fallback is not satisfied on its own terms (30 rather than 60–90 days' notice; no end-of-term Vendor convenience right), but that is irrelevant because the drafter's locked target is the preferred level, which is met.
